steps.title: Sterilize and grow seedlings
steps.instruction: Surface‑sterilize Arabidopsis seeds with 70 % ethanol, sow on vertical ½ MS square plates containing 1 % agar and grow for 10 days under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle. Lay plates horizontally in darkness for 2 days to promote upward hypocotyl growth, then return to the long‑day condition for another 2 days.

steps.title: Apply paraquat to seedlings
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL of 10 µM paraquat to each plate slowly so the solution spreads evenly over the media surface (enough to submerge the surface but not touch the leaves). Keep plates horizontally in darkness for 6 h. Harvest roots and leaves separately, rinse three times briefly with distilled water, blot dry with paper towels, and weigh (use similar weights for mutants and controls). Freeze the material in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Isolate and prepare protoplasts
steps.instruction: Prepare protoplasts from leaves of 4‑week‑old Arabidopsis grown under an 8 h light/16 h dark cycle (Yoo et al., 2007). Suspend the protoplasts in cold W5 buffer, count them with a hemocytometer, discard the W5 buffer and resuspend to a final concentration of 2 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹ using paraquat treatment solution. Use at least 10 mL of protoplast suspension per assay and incubate in darkness at room temperature for 3 h, gently shaking by hand every 20 min.

steps.title: Wash protoplasts after uptake
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 100 × g for 2 min at 4 °C, carefully remove the supernatant, add 10 mL wash buffer and gently resuspend. Repeat the centrifugation and wash two additional times (three washes total).

steps.title: Set up uptake/efflux assay
steps.instruction: After the final wash, resuspend protoplasts in wash buffer and aliquot equally into several tubes, each representing a time point (0, 10, 30, 60 min) with at least three replicates per point. Keep the tubes in darkness at room temperature and start a timer. At each time point, centrifuge as above, collect supernatant and pellet separately, then freeze the samples in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Extract paraquat from samples
steps.instruction: Place 1 × 10⁶–2 × 10⁶ protoplasts or 20–30 mg of plant tissue in a 2 mL centrifuge tube. Perform three freeze‑thaw cycles (freeze in liquid nitrogen for 1 min, thaw in a room‑temperature water bath for 2 min). For tissue, grind to a fine powder in liquid nitrogen. Add 800 µL paraquat extraction solution, sonicate on ice for a total of 20 min (1 min on/1 min off cycles), then incubate in a 60 °C water bath for 30 min and cool to room temperature. Centrifuge at 13 500 × g for 10 min at 4 °C and collect the supernatant. Repeat the addition of extraction solution, sonication, heating, and centrifugation, and combine all supernatants. Evaporate the organic solvents with a nitrogen‑blowing concentrator and store the dried residue at –80 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Redissolve extracts for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL room‑temperature redissolving solution to each dried sample in its 2 mL tube, flick the tube several times until fully dissolved, then centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Transfer 80 µL of the clear supernatant into a 2 mL amber screw‑vial equipped with a 150 µL liner pipe.

steps.title: UHPLC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µL of the prepared sample into a Waters BEH HILIC column (1.7 µm, 2.1 × 100 mm). Run a linear gradient at 0.4 mL min⁻¹: 0 min 90 % B; 1 min 90 % B; 2 min 20 % B; 4.3 min 20 % B; 4.5 min 90 % B; 7 min 90 % B. Detect in positive ESI‑MRM mode, setting ion source gas 1 = 55 psi, gas 2 = 55 psi, curtain gas = 35 psi, source temperature = 500 °C, spray voltage = 5 500 V. Monitor paraquat transitions 186.0→171.0 (quantification) and 93.2→171.3 (confirmation) with declustering potential = 100 V, collision energy = 60 V, and additional compound‑specific voltages 25 V and 17 V as required. Use default manufacturer settings for all other parameters. Integrate the target peak with a minimum width of 9 points, minimum height of 1 000 points, S/N threshold ≥ 3, and a baseline‑subtraction window of 2 min.

steps.title: Prepare W5 buffer
steps.instruction: Combine mother solutions to obtain final concentrations of 154 mM NaCl, 125 mM CaCl₂, 5 mM KCl, and 2 mM MES (pH 5.7). Filter the solution and store at 4 °C. Make fresh W5 buffer from the stored mother solutions as needed.

steps.title: Prepare paraquat treatment solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the same salt composition as W5 buffer and add 5 mM paraquat. Make the solution fresh from the stored mother solutions; store the paraquat mother solution at –4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Prepare wash buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare wash buffer with 154 mM NaCl, 125 mM CaCl₂, 5 mM KCl, and 2 mM MES (pH 5.7) using the stored mother solutions. Make fresh before use.

steps.title: Prepare paraquat extraction solution
steps.instruction: Mix 60 % methanol with 40 % 0.5 M HCl. Store the solution at –20 °C for up to three months.

steps.title: Prepare redissolving solution
steps.instruction: Combine 50 % acetonitrile with 50 % Milli‑Q water. Prepare fresh before use.

steps.title: Prepare LC mobile phase solvents
steps.instruction: Solvent A (pH 3.95): dissolve 100 mM NH₄OAc and add 0.5 % formic acid in water; make fresh before each run. Solvent B: acetonitrile.
